Subject: Exploring savings for our inference pipeline

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cobaltytics is evaluating the Optimize toolkit to reduce per-token spend on our customer-facing summarization pipeline. Two quick questions before we loop Procurement:

1) For a production model (Llama-3-13B family) serving ~120 qps at p95 latency target of 250ms, what savings should we expect from batching + prefix/KV cache vs just switching to an 8-bit quantized runtime?

2) How do you typically structure discounts for pilots where we commit to a 3-month pilot with a small committed spend and then decide on a 12-month reserved capacity?

We’d also like a simple cost/accuracy tradeoff recommendation — we’re sensitive to a 1–2% ROUGE drop.

If helpful, I can share our latency profile and a sample request distribution.

Best,
Alex
Alex Chen
Platform Lead — ML Engineering\Cobaltytics

Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:08:00 -0700

Alex — thanks for the concise list. Attaching a short scope workbook (Optimize_Toolkit_Scope.xlsx) and a sample latency profile you can drop into the sheet. High level answers inline, then a suggested pilot commercial structure.

Short answers:
- Batching + prefix/KV cache: in production workloads with high request reuse we typically see 30–60% effective token reduction on user-visible requests (depends on reuse rate and sequence length). For p95-sensitive pipelines that’s often the most predictable win because latency impact is small when configured conservatively.
- 8-bit quantization (dynamic/int8): typically 25–45% model compute reduction relative to float16 runtime; accuracy delta depends on the model and prompt distribution. For Llama-3-13B we’ve seen <1.5% ROUGE degradation on average with our per-customer calibration, but your prompts matter.
- Combined approach: caching + quantization compound — you can expect ~45–70% total unit-cost reduction in favorable cases; in conservative estimates use ~40% to model procurement.

Pilot commercial suggestion (3-month):
1) 3-month pilot with a $25k committed credit (applied monthly) — Redwood provides 20% off list on Optimize toolkit usage during pilot.
2) Technical scope: we include two quantization profiles (dynamic int8 and mixed-precision int8/16), a cache policy configuration, and two-day on-call for rollout week.
3) If you convert to a 12-month Reserved plan within 30 days of pilot end, stack an early-conversion rebate equal to 10% of projected first-year usage applied as credits.

Deliverables and asks:
- We’ll run an A/B calibration test (attached plan) to measure ROUGE impact and p95 latency with each quant profile.
- Please send the sample request histogram (we can also ingest the CSV you have).

CCing Karthik for quant/latency guidance and Mina on commercial guardrails.

Thanks,

Alex / team — quick technical note from the runtime side to set expectations for the A/B plan.

- Quant profiles: we recommend starting with dynamic int8 + a fallback fp16 path. Dynamic int8 gives the best throughput uplift with minimal model conversion time. For sensitive prompts we’ll run mixed-precision (int8 for attention + fp16 for FFN) as a second profile.
- Latency versus batch size: at 120 qps you’ll see latency improvements up to a point; because p95 target is tight (250ms), we’ll cap batching at ~16 tokens sequentially for user requests to avoid amplification of tail latency. The runtime telemetry will let us tune the batching window (we can deploy conservative defaults first).
- KV cache policy: for summarization where inputs have shared prefixes (e.g., repeated customer context) enable session-level prefix caching with a 6-hour TTL. That typically reduces tokens by ~20–40% on real-world SaaS traffic.
- Regression guardrail: our A/B uses task-level evals (ROUGE + custom semantic threshold) and an automated rollback if average quality drops >2% on your testset.

I’ve added a short checklist in the attached quantization_ab_test_plan.md. Mina — for the commercial team, pilot pricing is fine but can we offer a small additional operational credit ($5k) for integration hours? That’ll speed adoption.

Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
